idiom_name: libcurl curl_easy_header + curl_url resolver + hand-rolled RFC 8288 Link parser
implementation_notes: ISO C has no URI type, HTTP client, or link abstraction, so the link itself is a hand-written struct { char *href; char *rel; } plus an RFC 8288 Appendix B field-value parser over char*; what the C ecosystem supplies is the carrier and the resolver: libcurl's curl_easy_header (since 7.83) hands the application the raw Link: header value of a response (the CURLOPT_HEADERFUNCTION callback is the line-by-line fallback), and the curl_url interface parses the target URI and resolves a relative href against the request URL exactly as RFC 3986 Section 5 requires, with curl_url_get exposing scheme/host for policy checks before the link is dereferenced by a second easy transfer. The consumer's relation dispatch is a plain strcmp loop over the parsed links. This manual form stays justified in C because a full hypermedia client rarely fits embedded or systems footprints; when the payload side (HAL-style _links JSON) is needed instead of the header form, the canonical extension is a C JSON library feeding the same link struct, keeping the RFC 8288 header form for carriers that are not JSON bodies.
pitfalls: The curl_header struct returned by curl_easy_header is owned by the easy handle: its char* data is clobbered by the next curl_easy_header call on the same handle and freed only at curl_easy_cleanup, so a link list that stores the pointer instead of copying the bytes dangles as soon as the next header is read.

Every string produced by curl_url_get is allocated by libcurl and must be released with curl_free, never free(); mixing allocators across the library boundary is undefined behavior, and a link-following loop that forgets curl_url_cleanup leaks CURLU handles in long-running daemons.

Commas inside <...> targets and quoted-string parameters are legal, so a naive strtok(link_hdr, ",") splits valid link-values; RFC 8288 Appendix B requires quote-aware scanning, rel must not appear more than once per link-value, and a relative target must be resolved against the request URL - any base URI in the body is explicitly not applied.

curl_global_init must run once before any other libcurl call and is not thread-safe on platforms where curl_version_info lacks the threadsafe feature bit, so calling it from a link-following worker thread races the whole process; easy handles themselves must never be shared between threads.

Dereferencing a received link is not authorization: check the resolved scheme and host (curl_url_get with CURLUPART_SCHEME/CURLUPART_HOST) against an allowlist before curl_easy_perform, or a crafted rel="next" href turns your client into a pivot against internal services (SSRF).
